note: Feature list for maps. The site's Developers tab renders from this file at runtime. status: 'live' means it runs in this folder's playground today; 'planned' means it is not built and any code shown is a proposed API. 'tested' says what was actually checked at build time.

features.name: Globe and mercator rendering
features.summary: A WebGL globe with a one-call switch to flat mercator. Vector, raster and GeoJSON layers draw on both.
features.built: MapLibre GL JS 6.17.0 (BSD-3-Clause), vendored in this folder.
features.parity: Full for 2D layers. No proprietary 3D landmark or building styles.
features.tested: Rendered in headless Chrome at build.

features.name: Available bodies
features.summary: GlobeMap draws three round worlds - earth, moon and mars - chosen at construction or with setBody(); each carries its own base layers, Earth adds live overlays, and every layer is gated on a live probe before it draws. Irregular worlds like Phobos and Ganymede are drawn from a mesh by ShapeModel instead. The body and layer lists are introspectable at runtime (map.bodies, basesFor, overlaysFor), so the docs never drift from the code.
features.built: Round bodies share one MapLibre renderer (src/maps.js: the exported BODIES and the layer CATALOG). NASA Trek mosaics for the Moon and Mars are equirectangular; a small protocol rebuilds them as mercator tiles in the browser (src/eqproj.js, registered as gveq://), so no tile server sits in between. Irregular bodies use the separate ShapeModel renderer (src/shapemodel.js).
features.parity: Unique: no equivalent in general-purpose map SDKs. Limits: no polar caps beyond 85.05 degrees, and scale still assumes Earth's radius.
features.tested: Reprojection math checked against country borders with an Earth test image. Not yet seen with real NASA Trek tiles.

features.name: Irregular bodies: 3D shape models
features.summary: Not every world is a sphere. Phobos is a ~27 km lump with a crater (Stickney) nearly half its width, so you cannot map it on a globe at all. ShapeModel loads NASA's own glTF shape models and draws them as real meshes, with a latitude/longitude graticule and named features draped on the actual surface. Ganymede shows a big round world; Phobos shows one that is anything but.
features.built: src/shapemodel.js: a dependency-free glTF (.glb) loader and WebGL renderer. It parses the GLB container and its accessors, decodes the embedded texture with the browser's own createImageBitmap, lights and orbits the mesh, and derives the graticule and feature pins from the mesh geometry (a direction-to-radius grid), not the texture, so they hug the real lumpy surface. NASA shape models for Ganymede and Phobos are bundled under data/models/.
features.parity: Unique: general-purpose map SDKs assume a sphere or an ellipsoid and cannot represent a body like Phobos. Limits: this is a separate WebGL canvas, not a MapLibre layer, so the globe-only features (tiles, projections, the starfield) do not apply here; the named-feature coordinates are a small curated subset.
features.tested: Rendered in-browser: Phobos (16,449 verts / 32,040 tris) and Ganymede (10,604 verts) load in under 60 ms and draw with the graticule and pins. Phobos calibration checked against real geography: Stickney sits on the giant crater, Limtoc beside it, Hall at the south pole.

features.name: Hillshade and 3D terrain
features.summary: Shaded relief as a layer, and true 3D terrain when the camera is pitched.
features.built: MapLibre hillshade layer and setTerrain over Mapterhorn Terrarium tiles.
features.parity: Full.
features.tested: Not exercised at build: the terrain host was unreachable from the build sandbox.

features.name: Atmosphere
features.summary: A limb glow on the globe that fades out as you zoom in. Switched off on bodies without one.
features.built: MapLibre sky specification.
features.parity: Partial: fewer fog and lighting controls.
features.tested: Rendered in headless Chrome at build.

features.name: Celestial sky engine
features.summary: A real astronomical sky around each world: J2000 catalogue stars coloured by spectral type, the Milky Way on the true galactic plane, the Sun, Moon and planets by ephemeris, plus constellation lines, labels, an RA/Dec grid, the ecliptic, and a real day/night terminator on the globe. Each body is oriented by its IAU pole and prime meridian for any time, so the sky holds still while the planet turns inside it. The sky is observer-relative, so from Mars you see Earth, and the reachable worlds (Earth, Moon, Mars) are clickable travel hotspots: click one and the view flies to it and swaps the model.
features.built: src/celestial.js: a dependency-free, unit-tested engine (ICRF frames, IAU precession, obliquity, Sun/Moon/planet ephemerides via Standish + Meeus, galactic transform, B-V colour, proper motion). skyBodies(observer, date) recomputes the whole sky from the body you stand on. data/stars.json bundles 8,404 naked-eye stars (public-domain Yale Bright Star Catalogue, mag <= 6.5) with colour and proper motion. src/starfield.js projects it to MapLibre's globe with a calibrated pinhole camera and planet occlusion, draws the reachable worlds as DOM hotspot markers (CSS pulse, hover label, real clicks) whose click calls back into GlobeMap.travelTo(), and is shared by the SDK demo, the interactive playground (a 'Show the sky' toggle) and the landing-page hero globe.
features.parity: Unique: no general-purpose map SDK renders an astronomically-correct, time-aware sky with lit terminator. Positions are ICRF/J2000 with per-star proper motion applied for the epoch; nutation and aberration (sub-arcminute) are neglected. Pass addStarfield({ catalog }) to supply an even deeper catalogue.
features.tested: 22 astronomy checks pass in Node (equinox/solstice Sun, subsolar point, planet distances, full Moon, precession, galactic centre); proper motion verified (Sirius 1.34 arcsec/yr). In-browser: 8,404 stars render at ~3 ms/frame, Orion and Canis Major sit in the correct places, and the terminator shades the correct hemisphere.

features.name: Open basemap, no share-alike
features.summary: Land, borders and country labels from public-domain Natural Earth data, served from your own origin. Safe for a paid tier. Coarse by design: built for globe zooms.
features.built: Natural Earth 110m GeoJSON and Noto Sans glyphs (SIL OFL), both bundled.
features.parity: Partial: far less street detail than a commercial street basemap.
features.tested: Rendered in headless Chrome at build.

features.name: Satellite imagery
features.summary: Global imagery from sources that allow commercial use: NASA Blue Marble and the 2016 Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic.
features.built: MapLibre raster sources over NASA GIBS and EOX WMTS.
features.parity: Partial: about 10 m at best. No sub-metre commercial imagery.
features.tested: Not exercised at build. The Sentinel-2 entry was corrected on 2026-11-09 and awaits a re-probe.

features.name: Street detail (quarantined)
features.summary: Roads, water and place names from OpenStreetMap. It is share-alike data, so it is flagged, kept separate, and stripped from any paid style until counsel signs off.
features.built: MapLibre vector source over OpenFreeMap. Target: your own PMTiles archive on object storage.
features.parity: Partial: minimal styling today.
features.tested: Not exercised at build.

features.name: Time dimension
features.summary: Layers that take a date. The playground has daily VIIRS true color: pick a day, the tiles swap.
features.built: A {date} token in the manifest URL, swapped with setTiles.
features.parity: Partial: daily imagery today. Hourly model data needs the time-series pipeline.
features.tested: Not exercised at build. The entry was moved to the NOAA-20 layer on 2026-11-09 and awaits a re-probe.

features.name: Live feeds
features.summary: GeoJSON feeds drawn straight from the agency that publishes them. The playground shows the last day of USGS earthquakes, sized and colored by magnitude.
features.built: MapLibre GeoJSON source with data-driven circle styling.
features.parity: Full.
features.tested: Not exercised at build.

features.name: Wind and current particles
features.summary: Animated flow lines on the globe and in mercator. The renderer is live in the demo, driven by an illustrative analytic field; wiring it to real GFS/RTOFS data rides on the time-series pipeline. Pass your own field(lng,lat) to drive it from live data.
features.built: map.addParticles() in src/maps.js: a projection-aware canvas particle layer (works on globe and mercator). Candidate for the real-data path: WeatherLayers GL on deck.gl (MIT).
features.parity: Partial: renderer live; live forecast data is pending the time-series pipeline, so the default field is illustrative, not a forecast.
features.tested: Exercised in sdk-demo.html on both globe and mercator with the illustrative field.

features.name: Time-series animation
features.summary: Step a time-aware layer through its timesteps. Live today over the real NASA VIIRS daily mosaic; the GFS/RTOFS hourly pipeline (one cloud-optimized GeoTIFF per timestep with a STAC index) is the server-side next step.
features.built: map.timesteps()/setLayerTime()/playTimesteps() in src/maps.js animate the VIIRS daily source. Planned: COG per timestep + STAC index, served with Martin.
features.parity: Partial: daily imagery animation client-side; hourly model data needs the server pipeline.
features.tested: Exercised in sdk-demo.html: VIIRS stepped across seven days in headless Chrome.

features.name: Source manifest
features.summary: One file lists every source the map may contact, with its license, attribution, commercial flag and share-alike status. Code reads endpoints only from the manifest.
features.built: manifest.json in this folder.
features.parity: Unique: not offered as a developer feature elsewhere, as far as the research found.
features.tested: Loaded and rendered in headless Chrome at build.
features.code:
{
  "id": "eox-s2-2016",
  "kind": "raster",
  "body": "earth",
  "hosted": "third-party",

features.name: Live probes, no silent fallbacks
features.summary: Each source is requested once before its layer can be switched on. If it fails you see the status and the reason. Nothing is drawn in its place.
features.built: A fetch per manifest entry on load; layers are gated on the result.
features.parity: Unique.
features.tested: Verified at build: with third-party hosts unreachable, every dependent layer was disabled with a visible reason.

features.name: Dependency readout
features.summary: A running table of every host the page has contacted and how long each took. It is the dependency list, measured.
features.built: PerformanceObserver over resource timing.
features.parity: Unique.
features.tested: Rendered in headless Chrome at build.

features.name: Bring your own layer
features.summary: Drop in a GeoJSON, KML or GPX file, a PMTiles archive, a GeoTIFF or COG, or paste a file URL or an {z}/{x}/{y} raster tile template, and it draws on the globe, read in the browser, nothing uploaded.
features.built: map.addUserLayer() in src/maps.js routes by type: GeoJSON, XYZ raster, KML/GPX (parsed with the browser's own DOMParser), PMTiles (addPMTiles) and GeoTIFF/COG (addGeoTIFF). PMTiles and GeoTIFF are decoded natively in src/rasterformats.js with no extra libraries: PMTiles v3 header, Hilbert directories and gzip tiles over HTTP range requests or a dropped file; GeoTIFF/BigTIFF IFDs with none/Deflate/LZW/PackBits and the GeoKeys for footprint and CRS.
features.parity: GeoJSON, KML, GPX, XYZ raster, PMTiles (vector and raster) and GeoTIFF/COG (EPSG:4326 and 3857) are live. Other GeoTIFF projections need a gdalwarp first; WMS is still to come. No hosted upload service, by choice.
features.tested: src/rasterformats.js passes 48 Node checks (PMTiles header/directory/Hilbert/gzip, GeoTIFF IFD/geo-corners, Deflate/LZW/PackBits decode). Exercised end to end in sdk-demo.html: GeoJSON, XYZ, a PMTiles archive and a GeoTIFF added, fit, and removed in headless Chrome.

features.name: Build your own world
features.summary: Load a whole-planet equirectangular image as the globe's surface. A modeller can paint an imaginary planet (speculation, games, anything), export the texture, and map it here, wrapped on the sphere in the browser with no tile server. A downloadable template comes with it.
features.built: GlobeMap.sphereTemplate() generates a labelled plate-carree guide; map.addUserWorld() registers the painted image and the gvworld:// protocol in src/eqproj.js resamples it into Web Mercator tiles, the same technique that draws the Moon and Mars. data/planet-template.svg ships as a static template too.
features.parity: Unique: no general-purpose map SDK lets you wrap an arbitrary painted planet onto a live globe in the browser.
features.tested: Exercised in sdk-demo.html: the generated template was loaded as a world and wrapped onto the globe in headless Chrome.

features.name: Draw and measure
features.summary: Draw points, lines and polygons on the globe, with live geodesic length (km) and spherical area (km²). Click to add vertices; double-click or Enter finishes.
features.built: map.draw() in src/maps.js: a custom MapLibre interaction with haversine length and spherical-excess area. No extra libraries. Snapping and antimeridian-safe polygons are the next step.
features.parity: Partial: measurement and finish events today; snapping and per-feature styling to come.
features.tested: Exercised in sdk-demo.html: point, line and polygon drawn and measured in headless Chrome.

features.name: Place search
features.summary: Find places by name over the bundled Natural Earth index: place-name grade, self-hosted, nothing leaves the page. A global gazetteer (Photon over Overture and GeoNames) is the next step.
features.built: map.search() in src/maps.js ranks matches over the bundled Natural Earth names; map.flyToPlace() frames a result.
features.parity: Partial: bundled country and place names today, not a full address or global-gazetteer index.
features.tested: Exercised in sdk-demo.html: typed queries returned ranked matches and flew the camera to them in headless Chrome.

features.name: SDK
features.summary: One package that wraps the renderer, the manifest, probes, bodies and science layers. Create one object, switch worlds with one call, and every layer stays gated on its live probe. It ships in this folder and drives the live demo.
features.built: src/maps.js: a thin, dependency-free layer over MapLibre GL JS, the manifest and the gveq:// protocol.
features.parity: Unique: no general-purpose map SDK switches between Earth, Moon and Mars behind one object with per-layer license and probe gating.
features.tested: Runs end-to-end in sdk-demo.html: globe draws, probes gate layers, and body switching was exercised in headless Chrome.

features.name: Keys and metering (self-host)
features.summary: For self-hosters who want to put a metered gateway in front of their own tiles: API keys with per-key origin allow-lists, per-minute rate limits and usage counted per key. Shipped as reference code (serve.mjs + keys.mjs), not a hosted service — Rendered Data does not run a metered API for you.
features.built: keys.mjs + keys.json, served by serve.mjs on /v1. Each request is key-checked, origin-checked and rate-limited; usage totals and per-day counts persist to usage.json and survive a restart (a production build would run this at the edge).
features.parity: Partial: a persisted-usage redirect tile gateway today; signed keys and an edge deployment next.
features.tested: Verified with curl: 401 without a key, 403 on a disallowed origin, 302 to the resolved upstream tile, 429 past the per-minute limit, and usage counted per key and persisted across a server restart.
features.code:
# keys live in keys.json (public keys only); usage is counted per key.
GET /v1/tiles/{body}/{tileset}/{z}/{x}/{y}?key=gv_pk_...   # 302 → upstream tile, metered
GET /v1/usage?key=gv_pk_...                               # { total, thisMinute, remainingThisMinute, byDay }

# e.g.
curl -I 'http://localhost:8787/v1/tiles/earth/viirs/3/2/3?key=gv_pk_dev_local'

features.name: MCP server for agents
features.summary: An MCP server that lets an AI agent ask about the map's layers and licenses and get style-ready answers back, each with its license attached. Reads the same manifest and feature list the site uses.
features.built: mcp-server.mjs: a dependency-free Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC 2.0) over stdio or HTTP. Tools: list_layers, get_layer_license, get_style_url, search_place. sample_value (reading a value at a point and time) waits on the time-series pipeline.
features.parity: Unique in returning style-ready layers with license flags. Stdio and a minimal Streamable-HTTP/SSE transport today; sample_value next.
features.tested: Driven over both transports: a scripted stdio client, and HTTP POST (JSON and SSE responses) plus a GET event stream via curl: initialize, tools/list and all four tool calls correct.
features.code:
# stdio (default)
node mcp-server.mjs

# or HTTP + SSE: POST JSON-RPC to /mcp
MCP_HTTP_PORT=2091 node mcp-server.mjs

# tools exposed to the agent:
list_layers(status?)                 # id, group, status, commercial flag
get_layer_license(layer)             # license, attribution, commercial, share-alike, store
get_style_url(body, base)            # playground deep link + SDK call
search_place(query, body?)           # bundled, place-name grade
